title: Impact of COVID-19 Situation in China on Key Supply Chains for Singapore
what_it_is: Impact of COVID-19 Situation in China on Key Supply Chains for Singapore

sections.label: Supply chain disruption mitigation
sections.summary: Singapore does not anticipate major sustained supply chain disruptions, though short-term localised disruptions in China are possible, and companies are encouraged to maintain resilience plans.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
sentences.text: While we do not anticipate any major sustained disruptions in the supply chains of essential goods to Singapore, in the short term, we may see some localised disruptions in China's production capabilities and supply chains.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
sentences.text: However, over the past few years, companies in Singapore have strengthened their business continuity plans as well as supply chain resilience plans, and we encourage them to continue doing so, to mitigate supply chain disruptions.

sections.label: China import supply chain outlook
sections.summary: Singapore expects no major sustained supply chain disruption from China, but short-term localised disruptions are possible, and manufacturing and construction sectors have strengthened continuity plans, supplier diversification and inventory buffers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: Our sensing is, at this juncture, we are not expecting any major sustained, disruption in the supply chain of goods from China to Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: However, in the short term, that could be some localised disruptions in China's production capabilities and supply chains.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: Our key imports from China includes electronics and that is not disproportionate to the world.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: Electronics, machinery, metals and metal products, which are primarily used by the businesses in manufacturing and construction sector.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: Since early 2020, we have been working with these two sectors – in fact, with many other sectors – to future-proof themselves against supply chain disruption risks.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: One, they have strengthened their business continuity plans.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: They have also stepped up their supplier diversification and build up their inventory buffers to better prepare for any supply chain disruption.
